newsitem.title: UK: Inchcape first half profits flat, cuts dividend.
newsitem.headline: Inchcape first half profits flat, cuts dividend.

text.p: UK-based distribution group Inchcape Plc said on Monday its first half pre-tax profits were lower than last year at 82.8 million pounds ($128.6 million) and it slashed its interim dividend to 4.2p per share from 6.0p.
The results were around market expectations, after the company warned last May that profits would be slightly down.

Inchcape said the figures had benefited from its rationalisation programme, an upturn in some motors markets and strong performances from its bottling operation in Chile, Inchcape NRG and its Testing Services division.

Testing is one of the group's operations it plans to divest later this year. It said there had been "considerable interest" in the sale of the unit which raised its operating profits 37 percent to 15.7 million pounds in the first half.
The other business that Inchcape plans to divest, this time by demerger, is insurance broker Bain Hogg which saw operating profit dip 20 percent in the first half due to softening insurance rates.
"We are confident that the secind half, based on the business currently constituted, will show good recovery over the comparative period," said Inchcape chairman Colin Marshall."
He said this would lead to a rise in full-year ore-tax profits before exceptional costs. ($1=.6439 Pound)
